name: chess with commanding knights
description: Chess in which a knight can move the enemy's pieces. Any enemy piece other than the king that stands a knight's jump from one of your knights can be moved by you, on your turn and as your move for that turn, the way it always moves, but only to an empty square: you can never make it take anything. It stays its owner's piece, and its owner can still move it too. So a knight offers two things on every square it eyes: take the piece, or move it. Moving it is how to pull a defender off the square it guards, drag an enemy pawn forward where it can never come back, or step an enemy piece out of the way of your own attack and give a discovered check. A commanded piece never castles, captures in passing or promotes, and you may not move it so that your own king is left in check. Every piece a knight's jump from an enemy knight is on loan, so the knights' outposts matter more than in chess, and a defender has to ask not only what a knight attacks but what it could move.
